doc.title: Horn Shirley — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

title: Thinking of retirement and the toll of travel
summary: She would cut to one concert a month; a doctor told her to rest after years of flying.

story.theme_name: Still working: current gigs, upcoming projects and plans
story.community_name: What's next: upcoming tours, records and plans

blocks.x: Do you ever think of retiring?

Yeah, but my retirement‘s like maybe doing, next year I‘ll do one concert a month. That‘s enough, you know, because it‘s really been crazy. I mean, I‘ve done some . . . the last six years. For three years there I was traveling so much the doctor said, ―Well, you‘re going to have to chill, because you‘re getting some kind of weird,‖ from flying, meeting myself, passing myself, I mean, crossing Water Street four times. Like this is bad; it‘s bad on you. And I‘m getting old; I feel it. I‘m tired. I feel like somebody . . . who was it had the baseball bat on my . . . it‘s rough. But it‘s all about when you get involved with the music, you sit down to play with the guys, all that just goes right on out the window. And why did you stop singing?
Oh, [unclear] on me, well. Well, I‘ll tell you, I promise, at the end of the interview I‘ll tell you.

I know, I promise. I won‘t forget. I‘ll tell you, for sure. We‘ll go through it. I mean, it‘s not that big of a deal, but I‘ll make sure that I tell you, or you can talk me into singing. Maybe if you decide to give me lessons.
